source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 1 · lesson 20. Exercises reused from the lesson; du'aas flagged for review.

title.en: The Prophet's ﷺ kindness: a generous host

learn.en: The Prophet ﷺ always served food to his guests himself — Muslims and non-Muslims alike.
learn.title: A generous host

learn.en: Once he gave a guest all the food in his house, while he and his family stayed hungry.
learn.title: Giving everything

learn.en: A guest who was not yet a Muslim drank the milk of six goats — and the Prophet ﷺ kept serving him!
learn.title: Six goats of milk

learn.en: Diyafah means hospitality: treating a guest generously, whoever they are. It is part of good character.
learn.title: Diyafah

learn.en: “And indeed, you are of a great moral character.” (Qur'an 68:4)
learn.title: Great character

quiz.en: The Prophet ﷺ was always ___ to his guests.
The Prophet ﷺ ___ his guests himself.
The guest drank the milk of ___ goats.
True or false? The Prophet ﷺ was kind only to Muslim guests.

think.q: How can you be a generous host to a guest in your home this week?
think.a: Offer them a drink, share your snacks or toys, and serve them first!

parents.summary: The Prophet ﷺ served guests himself, Muslims and non-Muslims, even going hungry: hospitality (ḍiyāfa).
parents.tip: Next time you have guests, let him serve them and welcome them in Arabic.
